court: High Court of Judicature at Madras
trial_court: Additional District Munsif, Villupuram, O.S.No.76 of 2007
facts_of_case: The petitioner filed a suit in O.S.No.76 of 2007 against the respondents seeking declaration and perpetual injunction. The respondents resisted the petition to amend the plaint.

legal_principles.principle: An amendment changing the nature and character of the case cannot be allowed.
legal_principles.held: The Apex Court has also held that an amendment changing the nature and character of the case cannot be allowed.

legal_principles.principle: A party may rely on different rights alternatively and there is nothing in the Civil P.C. to prevent a party from making two or more inconsistent sets of allegations & claiming relief thereunder in the alternative.
legal_principles.held: Mukherjea, J, while penning down the judgment on behalf of a three judges bench of the Supreme Court has observed as under: 'A pltf., may rely upon different rights alternatively & there is nothing in the Civil P.C. to prevent a party from making two or more inconsistent sets of allegations & claiming relief thereunder in the alternative.'
cited_cases: Firm Sriniwas Ram Kumar Vs.Mahabir Prasad and others AIR (38) 1951 (SC)

legal_principles.principle: When the alternative case, which the pltf., could have made, was not only admitted by the deft., in his written statement but was expressly put forward as an answer to the claim which the pltf., made in the suit, there would be nothing improper in giving the pltf., a decree upon the case which the deft., himself makes.
legal_principles.held: Mukherjea, J, while penning down the judgment on behalf of a three judges bench of the Supreme Court has observed as under: 'When the alternative case, which the pltf., could have made, was not only admitted by the deft., in his written statement but was expressly put forward as an answer to the claim which the pltf., made in the suit, there would be nothing improper in giving the pltf., a decree upon the case which the deft., himself makes.'
cited_cases: Firm Sriniwas Ram Kumar Vs.Mahabir Prasad and others AIR (38) 1951 (SC)

legal_principles.principle: Amendments should be refused only where the other party cannot be placed in the same position as if the pleading had been originally correct, but the amendment would cause him an injury which could not be compensated in costs.
legal_principles.held: In North Eastern Railway Administration, Gorakhpur V.Bhagvan das (D) by Lrs) 2008-4-LW-80, while speaking on behalf of a Division Bench, Hon'ble Mr.Justice D.K.Jain has observed as under: 'Amendments should be refused only where the other party cannot be placed in the same position as if the pleading had been originally correct, but the amendment would cause him an injury which could not be compensated in costs.'
cited_cases: North Eastern Railway Administration, Gorakhpur V.Bhagvan das (D) by Lrs) 2008-4-LW-80

outcome.final_order: The impugned order was set aside.

use_for_drafting: understanding the role of notice in litigation
